answer: One concrete Sybil defense is slashable stake: to earn an identity, each agent locks an anchor of value as collateral, giving every vote a real price. Clones that mirror a single controller are caught by correlated keys and synchronized behavior, and a proven duplicate forfeits its entire bond. To buy k votes an attacker must lock k independent stakes, and detection slashes all of them, so cost scales linearly with the attack while the honest lagoon of rewards stays open to all. Forgery therefore never pays.
